title: An Exploration of Feasible Approaches to Soundscape and Music Therapy
research_question: To investigate the usage and validate the feasibility of combining soundscape and music therapy methods for workspace applications to improve working population stress and emotional state.

participants.description: Target population aged 20-40 years old, working population.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Soundscape created using audio equipment or tweaked on-site by a music therapist using Max/msp design soundscape improvisation tool. Includes three scenarios (forest, cliff, beach) and electroacoustic effects (granular delays, multichannel diffusion).

measures.instrument: Questionnaire (subjective assessment of pleasantness, unpleasantness, excitability)
Sound level meter, Acoustic Recording Units
Heart rate (HR), skin electrical activity (GSR), electroencephalography (EEG)
Perceptual devices (voice recording, headgear, smartphone apps)

mechanisms: Music has neural mechanisms capable of eliciting emotion, involving brain regions such as the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, and hippocampus, which can reduce stress and alleviate depression/anxiety.
Dopamine-related structures in the brain become active during enjoyable listening, suggesting music's pleasure is linked to dopamine release.
Acoustic roughness (fundamental frequency/harmonics near critical bandwidth) is a discordant and unpleasant aspect that causes a shift in emotion.
Off-key chords away from the tonal center create tension, influencing emotional states.
Autonomic nervous system changes (heart rate, respiratory rate, body temperature, galvanic skin responses) are characteristics that can identify emotional and physical changes associated with sound.
Emotion is frequently accompanied by physiological changes, allowing physiological indicators to provide an objective assessment of psychological state.
moderators: Target population's age range (20-40 years old)
General psychological state of the space (tense, calm)
implementation_implications: The proposed soundscape and music therapy intervention aims to improve the overall work environment and employee well-being, enabling employees to better cope with stress, increase productivity, and achieve a balance between work and life.

The design of this program can be combined with artificial intelligence methods after maturation to reduce intervention costs and integrate intervention effects, seeking future applications in various scenarios and spaces.
Soundscape intervention through data measurement and accumulation can be carried out via numerical values and keywords, potentially reducing the need for a music therapist.
limitations: The project necessitates a simulated workspace intervention initially, rather than an actual workspace, to analyze effects on stress. This implies the current stage is a design/simulation, not a real-world test.
Soundscape research technique remains limited in that there is no clear system of standardizing scales.
crossref_title: An Exploration of Feasible Approaches to Soundscape and Music Therapy
crossref_abstract: Stressful and strained workplace settings are becoming more common in modern culture, significantly affecting employees' mental well-being and work productivity. The purpose of this article is to investigate the usage of soundscape in the workplace using music therapy. We will cover the present state of soundscape development in conjunction with music therapy possibilities, as well as merging the good effects of soundscape with music therapy interventions to build a unique emotional intervention program. We will also look at crucial elements and testing methods to consider, as well as how these can be incorporated and examined early in the program design process. Most importantly, our research aims to validate the feasibility of soundscape combined with music therapy methods for workspace applications in the hope of improving working population stress and emotional state through intelligent interventions, thereby improving the overall work environment and employee well-being, enabling employees to better cope with stress, increase productivity, and achieve a balance between work and life.
